race_week_carb_loading.rationale: Current daily carbs: 464g (6.2 g/kg). Loading target: 747g/day (10 g/kg) for final 2 days to maximize muscle glycogen.

days.label: Race Day -3
days.focus: Normal training diet, start reducing fiber
days.fiber_note: Start reducing raw vegetables, legumes, high-fiber cereals.

days.label: Race Day -2
days.focus: Begin loading — increase carbs, reduce fiber and fat
days.fiber_note: Low fiber only (<20g). White rice, white bread, pasta, potatoes.
days.sodium_note: Increase sodium to 4000-5000 mg to aid glycogen storage and fluid retention.
meal_ideas: Breakfast: White bread with honey + banana + coffee
Lunch: White rice + grilled chicken + low-fiber vegetables
Dinner: Pasta with tomato sauce + lean protein
Evening: Fruit juice + white bread with peanut butter

days.label: Race Day -1
days.focus: Peak loading — maximum carbs, minimal fiber and fat
days.fiber_note: Very low fiber (<15g). Avoid salads, raw vegetables, beans entirely.
days.sodium_note: Keep sodium at 4000-5000 mg. Add salt to meals. Drink electrolyte mix between meals.
meal_ideas: Breakfast: Large bowl of white rice with honey + juice
Lunch: Pasta with simple sauce + white bread
Snack: Rice cakes + honey + electrolyte drink
Dinner (early, by 18:00): Smaller pasta portion + baked potato + juice
Evening: Low-fiber cereal with milk (settle stomach for morning)
days.important: Eat dinner early. Nothing new. Favor foods you've eaten before race days.

principles: Low fat, low fiber — easy to digest.
Familiar foods only — nothing new on race morning.
Sip 500-750 ml water with electrolytes alongside the meal.

recommended_meal.description: Based on your tracked breakfast/pre-workout foods

option_a.name: Oatmeal + banana (your training breakfast)
option_a.note: Closest to your brick-day breakfast. Oatmeal has moderate fiber — eat earlier (3 hrs) if GI-sensitive.

option_b.name: White bread + PB (your long-ride breakfast)
option_b.note: Lower fiber than oatmeal. Good if eating 2.5 hrs before start.

top_up.items: 1 gel (25g carbs) + 200ml water or sports drink
top_up.note: Quick-absorbing carbs to top off blood glucose. Already in your routine.

swim.nutrition: None during swim. Focus on pacing and sighting.

t1.nutrition: Sip electrolyte drink while transitioning. No solid food.

what_to_carry: 2-3 bottles (500-750ml each) of sports drink mix
Top tube or bento box for gels
3 gels in race belt (1 caffeinated for km 15+)
Rely on aid station drinks for fluid
Salt capsules (2-3) as backup if cramping

fueling_gap_analysis.recommendation: Your current training fueling rate is ~56 g/hr. Race target is 85 g/hr on the bike — that is a significant increase of 29 g/hr. Practice higher intake in long rides over the next weeks to train your gut.

sweat_rate_estimate.estimated_from: Cronometer biometric weight changes around long sessions

observations.note: Lower post-long-ride weigh-in reflects fluid loss, not fat loss — relevant if this feeds a sweat-rate estimate.

sweat_rate_estimate.estimated_sweat_rate_L_per_hr: ~1.0-1.5 L/hr (estimated from weight delta, but confounded by food/fluid intake during session)
sweat_rate_estimate.recommendation: Perform a controlled sweat test: weigh pre/post a 1-hour run in similar heat, track fluid intake. This gives a precise per-hour rate.
sweat_rate_estimate.caveat: Weight change post-workout reflects fluid loss minus fluid intake during workout. Not a clean sweat rate without controlling for intake.

key_reminders: Nothing new on race day — only foods and products tested in training.
Front-load bike nutrition: take your first gel/drink within 10 min of starting the bike.
Set 20-min alerts on your bike computer as fueling reminders.
If GI distress on the run: switch to small sips of cola + water only.
Tropical heat increases fluid and sodium needs — err on the higher end of ranges.
Weigh yourself before and after key training sessions to calibrate your personal sweat rate.
Caffeine: first caffeinated gel no earlier than the second half of the bike.
These are sports-nutrition heuristics based on your tracked data, not medical advice.
